description: unxz and xzcat are aliases for decompression; lzma, unlzma and lzcat select the legacy .lzma format.

option.name: --arm
tip: Add an ARM BCJ filter to the filter chain.
Valid OPTS: start=NUM; the value must be attached with =.
Can only be used as a non-last filter in the chain.

option.name: --arm64
tip: Add an ARM64 BCJ filter to the filter chain.
Valid OPTS: start=NUM; the value must be attached with =.
Can only be used as a non-last filter in the chain.
4096-byte alignment is best for ARM64.

option.name: --armthumb
tip: Add an ARM-Thumb BCJ filter to the filter chain.
Valid OPTS: start=NUM; the value must be attached with =.
Can only be used as a non-last filter in the chain.

option.name: --best
tip: Use compression preset 9.
The --best spelling is a backwards-compatible alias for -9; avoid using it.

option.name: --block-list
tip: Start a new .xz block after the given comma-separated intervals of uncompressed data.
Each item is an optional filter chain number 0-9 followed by a colon and a size.
An omitted item reuses the previous item; a final 0 means the rest of the file.

option.name: --block-size
tip: Start a new .xz block after every SIZE bytes of input.
Use this to set the block size for threaded compression.
The default is three times the LZMA2 dictionary size or 1 MiB, whichever is greater.

option.name: --check
tip: Set the integrity check type.
Possible values: none, crc32, crc64, sha256.
The default is crc64; this affects only the .xz format.
none disables the integrity check and is usually a bad idea.

option.name: --compress
tip: Force compression.
This is the default operation mode when no mode option is given and the command name does not imply another mode.

option.name: --decompress
tip: Decompress.

option.name: --delta
tip: Add the Delta filter to the filter chain.
Valid OPTS: dist=NUM (1-256; default 1); the value must be attached with =.
The Delta filter can only be used as a non-last filter.

example.desc: Apply the Delta filter before LZMA2.

option.name: --extreme
tip: Try to improve compression ratio by using more CPU time.
Does not affect decompressor memory requirements.

option.name: --fast
tip: Use compression preset 0.
The --fast spelling is a backwards-compatible alias for -0; avoid using it.

option.name: --files
tip: Read filenames to process from FILE; if FILE is omitted, read them from standard input.
Filenames must be terminated with a newline; a dash is a regular filename, not standard input.
The value must be attached with =.

option.name: --files0
tip: Like --files but filenames are terminated with the null character.
The value must be attached with =.

option.name: --filters
tip: Set the full filter chain using the liblzma filter string syntax.
Use --filters-help for the syntax and supported filters.
A preset 0-9[e] can be used instead of a chain.

example.desc: Use an x86 BCJ filter followed by LZMA2.

option.name: --filters-help
tip: Display help for the liblzma filter string syntax and exit.

option.name: --filters1
tip: Set filter chain 1 using the liblzma filter string syntax.
Used with --block-list; use --filters-help for the syntax.

option.name: --filters2
tip: Set filter chain 2 using the liblzma filter string syntax.
Used with --block-list; use --filters-help for the syntax.

option.name: --filters3
tip: Set filter chain 3 using the liblzma filter string syntax.
Used with --block-list; use --filters-help for the syntax.

option.name: --filters4
tip: Set filter chain 4 using the liblzma filter string syntax.
Used with --block-list; use --filters-help for the syntax.

option.name: --filters5
tip: Set filter chain 5 using the liblzma filter string syntax.
Used with --block-list; use --filters-help for the syntax.

option.name: --filters6
tip: Set filter chain 6 using the liblzma filter string syntax.
Used with --block-list; use --filters-help for the syntax.

option.name: --filters7
tip: Set filter chain 7 using the liblzma filter string syntax.
Used with --block-list; use --filters-help for the syntax.

option.name: --filters8
tip: Set filter chain 8 using the liblzma filter string syntax.
Used with --block-list; use --filters-help for the syntax.

option.name: --filters9
tip: Set filter chain 9 using the liblzma filter string syntax.
Used with --block-list; use --filters-help for the syntax.

option.name: --flush-timeout
tip: Flush pending input when more than NUM milliseconds have passed and reading more input would block.
Use 0 to disable; this feature is not available on non-POSIX systems.

option.name: --force
tip: Overwrite the target file and (de)compress links.
With --decompress --stdout, copy unrecognized input unchanged so xzcat behaves like cat.

option.name: --format
tip: Set the file format to encode or decode.
Possible values: auto, xz, lzma, alone, lzip, raw.
auto is the default for xz; the lzma, unlzma and lzcat aliases default to lzma.
alone is a backwards-compatible alias for lzma.
lzip accepts .lz files when decompressing; compression is not supported.
raw requires an explicit filter chain and, without standard output, an explicit suffix.

option.name: --help
tip: Display the short help and exit.

option.name: --ia64
tip: Add an IA-64 (Itanium) BCJ filter to the filter chain.
Valid OPTS: start=NUM; the value must be attached with =.
Can only be used as a non-last filter in the chain.

option.name: --ignore-check
tip: Do not verify the integrity check of compressed data when decompressing.
The CRC32 values in the .xz headers are still verified.
Do not use this option unless you know what you are doing.

option.name: --info-memory
tip: Display total RAM and the active memory usage limits, then exit.

option.name: --keep
tip: Do not delete the input files.
Also processes symlinks, hard-linked files and files with setuid, setgid or sticky bits.

option.name: --list
tip: Print information about compressed files.
Use --verbose for more detail and --robot --list for machine-readable output.

option.name: --long-help
tip: Display the long help with all options and exit.

option.name: --lzma1
tip: Add an LZMA1 filter to the filter chain.
LZMA1 is supported mainly for the legacy .lzma format and cannot be used with .xz.
Can only be used as the last filter in the chain.
OPTS is a comma-separated list; the value must be attached with =.

example.desc: Use LZMA1 preset 6 with an 8 MiB dictionary.

option.name: --lzma2
tip: Add an LZMA2 filter to the filter chain.
LZMA2 is the filter used by .xz and can only be the last filter in the chain.
OPTS is a comma-separated list; the value must be attached with =.

example.desc: Use LZMA2 preset 6 with an 8 MiB dictionary.

option.name: --memlimit
tip: Set the memory usage limit for compression, decompression and multi-threaded decompression.
LIMIT can be bytes with a suffix, a percentage of RAM, 0 or max.
The --memory spelling is an alias.

option.name: --memlimit-compress
tip: Set the memory usage limit for compression.
LIMIT can be bytes with a suffix, a percentage of RAM, 0 or max.
If the limit is exceeded, xz adjusts the settings downwards unless --no-adjust is used.

option.name: --memlimit-decompress
tip: Set the memory usage limit for decompression.
This also affects --list.

option.name: --memlimit-mt-decompress
tip: Set the memory usage limit for multi-threaded decompression.
It only affects the number of threads and never makes xz refuse to decompress.
A value of 0 resets the system-specific default.

option.name: --no-adjust
tip: Display an error and exit if the memory usage limit cannot be met without adjusting output-affecting settings.
The number of threads may still be reduced.

option.name: --no-sparse
tip: Do not create sparse files when decompressing.
By default xz tries to make the output sparse when it contains long runs of zeros.

option.name: --no-sync
tip: Do not synchronize the target file and its directory to the storage device before removing the source file.
Improves performance for many small files, but a crash can leave neither file.

option.name: --no-warn
tip: Do not set the exit status to 2 for warnings.
This does not affect verbosity; use --quiet to hide warnings.

option.name: --powerpc
tip: Add a PowerPC BCJ filter to the filter chain.
Valid OPTS: start=NUM; the value must be attached with =.
Can only be used as a non-last filter in the chain.
Big endian only.

option.name: --quiet
tip: Suppress warnings and notices.
Specify twice to suppress errors too; this does not change the exit status.

option.name: --riscv
tip: Add a RISC-V BCJ filter to the filter chain.
Valid OPTS: start=NUM; the value must be attached with =.
Can only be used as a non-last filter in the chain.

option.name: --robot
tip: Print messages in a machine-parsable format.
Supported with --list, --filters-help, --info-memory and --version.

option.name: --single-stream
tip: Decompress only the first .xz stream and silently ignore remaining input.
This has no effect outside --decompress or --test and implies --keep since xz 5.7.1alpha.

option.name: --sparc
tip: Add a SPARC BCJ filter to the filter chain.
Valid OPTS: start=NUM; the value must be attached with =.
Can only be used as a non-last filter in the chain.

option.name: --suffix
tip: Use .SUF as the suffix for compressed files instead of .xz or .lzma.
The default is .xz, or .lzma for the lzma aliases.
When decompressing, recognize this suffix in addition to .xz, .txz, .lzma, .tlz and .lz.
A raw stream requires an explicit suffix unless writing to standard output.

option.name: --test
tip: Test the integrity of compressed files.
No files are created or removed; this is equivalent to --decompress --stdout with the output discarded.

option.name: --threads
tip: Use at most NUM worker threads.
0 uses as many threads as there are processor cores; 1 selects single-threaded mode; +1 forces multi-threaded mode with one thread.
The default is 0.

option.name: --to-stdout
tip: Write the compressed or decompressed data to standard output.
This implies --keep.

option.name: --verbose
tip: Be verbose; specify twice for even more detail.
A progress indicator is shown when standard error is a terminal.

option.name: --version
tip: Display the version number and exit.

option.name: --x86
tip: Add an x86 BCJ filter to the filter chain.
Valid OPTS: start=NUM; the value must be attached with =.
Can only be used as a non-last filter in the chain.

example.desc: Apply the x86 BCJ filter before LZMA2.
